value.rationale: The exact law is a quantitative Birkhoff-type theorem for a natural singular 2-adic odometer observable obtained from resonant proportional-delay feedback, with a parameter-uniform total-variation rate. The sharp moment threshold characterizes when this noncontinuous observable is Haar-integrable and quantifies a logarithmically divergent endpoint along an explicit orbit. It explains why the finite-horizon RMS and envelope tests can diverge even as typical-time occupation settles. The theorem is motivated by a 2026 paper rather than by an arbitrary arithmetic slice.
